routes-nav-8.title: Auth callback redirects to unvalidated ?next= value
routes-nav-8.description: auth/callback/route.ts:8-16 takes `next` straight from the query string and does NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}${next}`). Because origin is prefixed it is not a cross-origin open redirect, but the value is unvalidated: an absolute URL (next=https://evil.com) produces the malformed URL `http://host:porthttps://evil.com`, making NextResponse.redirect throw a 500, and arbitrary junk paths are accepted. Every other redirect target in the auth flow is validated (safeInternalPath in (auth)/actions.ts:16-25 and the sign-in page's check at (auth)/sign-in/page.tsx:31-32) — this route is the one gap. Security hardening, no auth-flow change.
routes-nav-8.fix: In src/app/auth/callback/route.ts, validate `next` the same way as safeInternalPath: if it is missing, doesn't start with "/", or starts with "//", fall back to the existing default ("/reset-password" for type=recovery, else "/dashboard") before redirecting.

ui-ux-1.title: ink-600 / ink-800 utility classes do not exist in the theme — ~120 usages across 60 files silently render unstyled
ui-ux-1.description: The Tailwind v4 @theme block in src/app/globals.css (lines 83-91) registers ink-50/100/200/300/400/500/700/900 only — there is no --color-ink-600 or --color-ink-800. Yet `text-ink-600`, `text-ink-800`, `hover:text-ink-800`, `bg-ink-100 text-ink-600`, and `hover:bg-ink-800` are used ~120 times across ~60 files (verified by grep). I confirmed against the dev server's compiled CSS (curl http://localhost:8080 → /_next/static/chunks/...css): zero `.text-ink-600`, `.text-ink-800`, or `.bg-ink-800` rules are generated, while `.text-ink-700` exists. Concrete breakage: workspace-shell.tsx:122 inactive section tabs (`text-ink-600`) inherit full-strength ink-900 instead of muted; segmented-tabs.tsx:44 `hover:text-ink-800` does nothing; confirm-dialog.tsx:133 the dark primary button's `hover:bg-ink-800` gives no hover feedback; profile-menu.tsx:130,144 menu items, terms/privacy body copy (`text-ink-800`), notifications empty-state title, support tickets table title links, dashboard hero/upcoming-content, community discussion-list, posting and notes components are all affected. (One affected file, src/components/tutorials/lesson-tabs.tsx:105,284, is files-off-limits — owned by another active session — but the fix below does not touch it.)
ui-ux-1.fix: In src/app/globals.css add two primitives to the :root palette after `--ink-500` (line ~40): `--ink-600: #57514A;` and after `--ink-700`: `--ink-800: #2A2724;` (interpolated between the existing 500→700→900 steps). Then register them in the @theme inline block next to the other ink entries (line ~89): `--color-ink-600: var(--ink-600);` and `--color-ink-800: var(--ink-800);`. No component edits needed — all 120 existing class usages start resolving.
ui-ux-1.verdictReasoning: Verified end-to-end. The @theme inline block in src/app/globals.css (lines 84-91) registers only ink-50/100/200/300/400/500/700/900; --color-ink-600 and --color-ink-800 are not defined in any CSS file in the repo (checked all of src/styles/tokens/* and dev-dashboard.css), there is no tailwind.config.* and no @config directive, and the :root primitives also lack --ink-600/--ink-800. Independently confirmed in compiled output (.next/dev/static/chunks/src_app_globals_css...css): .text-ink-700/.text-ink-900/.bg-ink-700 are generated but .text-ink-600, .text-ink-800, and .bg-ink-800 do not exist — Tailwind v4 silently drops utilities for unregistered theme keys. All cited component lines verified verbatim (workspace-shell.tsx:122 inactive nav tabs, segmented-tabs.tsx:44 hover:text-ink-800, confirm-dialog.tsx:133 hover:bg-ink-800, profile-menu.tsx:130/144). The auditor actually UNDERcounted: 193 occurrences across 100 files (vs claimed ~120/60). Impact is cosmetic-only (text inherits ink-900 from body, so it stays readable and contrast increases), but it collapses the entire muted/secondary text tier of the design system on every page including the persistent app shell, and kills hover feedback on primary dark buttons and tabs — high is justified within a ui-ux audit. The proposed fix is correct and minimal: the suggested hexes are within 1-2 RGB units of the true 500→700 and 700→900 midpoints, and it follows the file's existing :root-primitive + @theme-inline-registration pattern exactly, requiring no component edits and not touching the off-limits lesson-tabs.tsx.

ui-ux-3.title: Missions Activity tab shows hardcoded fake challenge progress ('3 of 7 days completed') to every user
ui-ux-3.description: mission-activity.tsx lines 309-310 define `CHALLENGE_TOTAL_DAYS = 7; CHALLENGE_COMPLETED_DAYS = 3;`. These constants drive both the 'Active Challenge' stat card (lines 155-180, '3 / 7 days completed' with a 43% progress bar) and the large ChallengeBanner (lines 312-437: 'Active Challenge · Day 3 of 7', a 7-step day tracker with days 1-3 checked, and '4 days left'). Every user sees identical, never-changing fake progress on /missions?tab=activity, directly beside real data (the activity chart, streak and points are all computed from the missions table in missions/page.tsx). 'Continue Challenge' links to /missions?tab=tasks, so the loop never updates what it claims to track.
ui-ux-3.fix: In src/components/missions/mission-activity.tsx, derive challenge progress from data already passed as props: compute `completedDays = streakLast7.filter(d => d.done).length` (or pass a dedicated last-7-day completion count from missions/page.tsx, which already buckets daily mission completions) and use it in place of CHALLENGE_COMPLETED_DAYS in both the StatCard and ChallengeBanner. Alternatively hide the Active Challenge card + banner entirely until a real challenge feature exists.
ui-ux-3.correctedFix: The proposed primary fix is semantically wrong: streakLast7.filter(d => d.done).length is a rolling 7-calendar-day activity count, not challenge progress. Progress would decrease as active days fall out of the window, "Day N of 7" and "X days left" would be incoherent (the challenge could regress or never complete), and the sequential day tracker would check the first N circles regardless of which days were actually active — replacing one fake display with another. Since no challenge entity (start date/enrollment) exists in the schema, true progress cannot be derived from existing props. Correct fix: adopt the auditor's stated alternative — remove or hide the Active Challenge StatCard (mission-activity.tsx lines 155-180) and ChallengeBanner (lines 183, 312-437), and also update the teaser copy in src/components/missions/missions-overview.tsx (line 147) that advertises "the 7-Day Challenge", until a real challenge feature with persisted state exists. If a live number is required without schema changes, Math.min(streakCurrent, 7) at least matches consecutive-posting-day semantics, but hiding is the honest, least-invasive option given the project's strict editing-scope rules.
ui-ux-3.verdictReasoning: Verified directly in source. mission-activity.tsx lines 309-310 hardcode CHALLENGE_TOTAL_DAYS = 7 and CHALLENGE_COMPLETED_DAYS = 3; the Active Challenge StatCard (lines 155-180) and the prop-less ChallengeBanner (lines 312-437) render "3 / 7 days completed", a 43% bar, "Active Challenge · Day 3 of 7", days 1-3 checked, and "4 days left" for every user, never changing. All sibling data on the same tab (activity series, streak, points, week total) is genuinely computed from the missions table in missions/page.tsx, so the fake card is indistinguishable from real data. A repo-wide grep confirms no challenges table, no enrollment state, and no server logic backing this — the only SQL hits are unrelated MFA-challenge audit events. missions-overview.tsx line 147 even advertises the 7-Day Challenge. The claim is fully reproduced and not mitigated elsewhere. However, severity is overstated: it is misleading static placeholder UI with no functional, data-integrity, or security impact — medium, not high.

ui-ux-4.title: Notifications dropdown is fixed 380px wide and overflows off-screen on mobile
ui-ux-4.description: notifications-dropdown.tsx line 227 renders the panel as `absolute right-0 ... w-[380px]` with no max-width. The bell trigger is rendered in the MOBILE topbar (topbar.tsx line 72) roughly 50-60px from the right screen edge, so on a 360-390px viewport the panel's left edge lands off-screen and is clipped by the global `body { overflow-x: hidden }` (globals.css lines 145-147) — notification text and the left edge of every row are cut off and unreachable. The dev-dashboard's equivalent dropdown already guards against this with `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]` (src/components/dev-dashboard/dev-notifications-dropdown.tsx line 249), proving the pattern is known.
ui-ux-4.fix: In src/components/app-shell/notifications-dropdown.tsx line 227 change the panel class to include a viewport clamp, mirroring the dev dropdown: `w-[380px] max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]` and adjust anchoring so it stays on-screen (e.g. `right-0` is fine once max-width caps it; or use `fixed inset-x-4` below the topbar on <sm).
ui-ux-4.correctedFix: Adding `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]` alone is NOT sufficient, and the auditor's claim that "right-0 is fine once max-width caps it" is wrong. The bell's right edge sits ~66px from the viewport right edge in the mobile topbar (44px avatar link + 6px gap + 16px padding are to its right), so a panel capped at calc(100vw-2rem) anchored right-0 still has its left edge at 32-66 = -34px — still clipped. (The referenced dev dropdown has the same residual defect: its bell also has a user chip to its right.) A correct fix must both cap the width and shift the anchor on small screens. Option A (pure CSS, matches the fixed mobile layout): change line 227's classes to `absolute -right-[50px] sm:right-0 top-[calc(100%+8px)] w-[380px] max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] ...` — the -50px (44px avatar + 6px gap) puts the panel's right edge at the 16px content padding, and the max-width cap then puts the left edge at exactly 16px from the viewport edge. Option B: on <sm use fixed positioning (`fixed inset-x-4 top-[calc(var(--mobile-topbar-height)+4px)] w-auto sm:absolute sm:inset-x-auto sm:right-0 sm:top-[calc(100%+8px)] sm:w-[380px]`) — but note the header's `backdrop-blur` (backdrop-filter) makes the header the containing block for fixed-position descendants; this happens to be harmless here because the header is full-width and sticky at top 0, but it should be verified visually. Option A is lower-risk.
ui-ux-4.verdictReasoning: All cited evidence reproduces. (1) src/components/app-shell/notifications-dropdown.tsx line 227 renders the panel as `absolute right-0 top-[calc(100%+8px)] w-[380px]` with no max-width, anchored to the 40px bell wrapper (`<div ref={ref} className="relative">`). (2) topbar.tsx line 72 renders NotifDropdown inside the `lg:hidden` mobile bar's right cluster: to the bell's right sit a gap-1.5 (6px), the avatar link (36px avatar + p-1 = 44px), and `--mobile-content-x` padding (clamp(1rem,4vw,1.25rem) = 16px on phones, defined in src/styles/tokens/containers.css line 31). ui-ux-5.title: Dashboard Performance tile renders follower DECLINES as green '▲ +x%' growth

The inner Math.abs is the divide-by-zero guard, not sign-stripping; removing it is only incidentally safe because followersSeries clamps to non-negative via `r.followers ?? 0`. Then in src/components/dashboard/launcher-tiles.tsx PerformanceCard (~line 434), branch on sign: `deltaPct >= 0` → "▲" with text-emerald-600, else "▼" with text-rose-600 (or a muted tone), rendering `Math.abs(deltaPct).toFixed(1)` for the number in both branches.

So follower declines do render as a green up-arrow "growth" badge. However, severity is overstated: the bug is purely presentational (the magnitude shown is correct, only the direction indicator is wrong), the sparkline drawn immediately below plots the real series so a decline is visibly trending down next to the badge, and there is no security/data-integrity impact. performance-1.verdictReasoning: Reproduced every element of the claim from the code. (1) src/components/marketing/proven-results.tsx renders raw tags at lines 133-137 (desktop accordion) and 204-208 (mobile stack), each preceded by an explicit `eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element` — the lint rule that exists to catch exactly this was deliberately suppressed. (2) STATS (lines 32-37) references the four %20-encoded /public JPEGs; measured sizes match the claim byte-for-byte: Posting.jpg 3,881,391 + Users Img.jpg 2,849,818 + Grow audience.jpg 2,148,882 + Less time spent.jpg 944,796 = 9,824,887 B (~9.37 MB). Both the `hidden lg:flex` desktop block and the `lg:hidden` mobile block render unconditionally (responsive via CSS only), and display:none elements still download per standard browser behavior, with no loading="lazy" attribute, so every visitor on every viewport eagerly downloads all ~9.4 MB. One small precision note: each file is referenced twice in the DOM but downloads once (browsers dedupe same-URL requests) — the claim's ~9.4 MB total is correct, it is not doubled. Refutation attempts all failed: next.config.ts has no images config (optimizer is available, not disabled); src/proxy.ts:40 explicitly excludes .jpg/_next/image from its matcher so it does nothing for these assets; Next 16.2.6's bundled docs (01-app/03-api-reference/02-components/image.md) confirm next/image with `fill` works exactly as the fix assumes (parent must be positioned — the desktop wrapper span is `absolute inset-0` and the mobile parent div has `relative`, both satisfied); and cta.tsx lines 30-36 confirms the project already uses next/image with fill+sizes for a comparable 3.4 MB JPEG, so the fix matches established project convention. Severity high is justified: ~9.4 MB of eager image transfer on the anonymous marketing landing page is the dominant performance cost of the entire route and directly damages LCP and bandwidth for every prospective customer.

performance-2.title: getShellContext runs 5 sequential Supabase round trips on every authenticated page
performance-2.description: getShellContext (lines 10-101) awaits, strictly in series: auth.getUser() → profiles select (line 17) → notifications count (line 41) → missions count (line 56) → social_accounts select (line 68). The last four are mutually independent (all only need user.id). This helper is called by src/app/(app)/layout.tsx line 17 and by every (app) page, so every dashboard/posting/programs/etc. render pays 4 unnecessary serial DB round trips (~100-300 ms of avoidable latency at typical 30-80 ms/query from a serverless region). It is React cache()-wrapped so it only runs once per request — the problem is purely the internal waterfall.
performance-2.fix: In src/lib/app-shell/get-shell-context.ts, after the auth.getUser() call, wrap the four independent queries in a single Promise.all: const [profileRes, notifCountRes, taskCountRes, socialRes] = await Promise.all([...]) preserving the existing try/catch fail-soft semantics (move each count query into a .then/.catch or a small helper that swallows errors and returns 0). No behavior change — same data, one round trip of latency instead of four.
performance-2.verdictReasoning: Verified in src/lib/app-shell/get-shell-context.ts: five strictly sequential awaits (auth.getUser line 14, profiles 17-23, notifications count 41-45, missions count 56-60, social_accounts 68-71); the last four depend only on user.id and are mutually independent, so the internal waterfall is real. src/app/(app)/layout.tsx line 17 awaits getShellContext with no Suspense boundary, so the waterfall blocks first paint of the entire shell on every authenticated page (~28 pages call it; React cache() dedupes to once per request as the claim concedes). src/proxy.ts only refreshes the auth cookie and cannot mitigate. The proposed Promise.all fix works: postgrest-js builders are lazy thenables so Promise.all parallelizes them, and I confirmed in node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/index.mjs (v2.105.4) that builders never reject by default (fetch errors are converted to {error, count: null} responses; shouldThrowOnError defaults to false), so the existing try/catch blocks are dead code and plain Promise.all preserves the fail-soft behavior exactly — the suggested .catch helpers are harmless but unnecessary. Severity pushback: only 3 round trips of latency are avoidable, not 4 (the profile query still costs one RTT), giving roughly 20-90 ms same-region to ~100-240 ms worst case of constant per-request latency. No correctness, scaling, or N+1 dimension — it does not grow with data. A constant ~100-250 ms TTFB cost with a trivial safe fix is a medium-severity latency issue, not high.

performance-3.fix: In src/app/(app)/community/page.tsx restructure the feed branch: keep `const posts = active === 'feed' ? await listRecentPosts(20) : []`, then when posts.length > 0 run `const [repliesByPost, votesByPost, reactionsByPost, attachmentsByPost, pollsByPost, isAdminRes, spaces] = await Promise.all([listRepliesForPosts(ids, ctx.user.id), getPostVotes(...), getPostReactions(...), getPostAttachments(ids), getPostPolls(...), (await createClient()).rpc('is_admin'), listSpaces()])`. Move listSpaces into the batch (it is currently awaited unconditionally at line 80 before anything else). Keep the existing fallbacks for non-feed tabs.
performance-3.correctedFix: The proposed fix gates the Promise.all batch — including listSpaces — behind posts.length > 0. That breaks the empty-feed case: with zero posts, spaces would be empty, so spaceOptions fed to InlineComposer (page.tsx line 138) would be empty and users in a brand-new community could not pick a space to create the first post (violates the project's "do not remove existing functionality" rule). The gate is also unnecessary: every per-post helper in src/lib/community/queries.ts already early-returns an empty Map with zero network calls when postIds.length === 0 (lines 192, 267, 298, 405-406, 461-462). Correct restructure for the feed branch, ungated: (1) Level 1 — `const supabase = await createClient(); const [spaces, posts, isAdminRes] = await Promise.all([listSpaces(), active === "feed" ? listRecentPosts(20) : Promise.resolve([]), active === "feed" ? supabase.rpc("is_admin") : Promise.resolve(null)]); const isAdmin = isAdminRes?.data === true;` (2) Level 2 — `const ids = posts.map(p => p.id); const [repliesByPost, votesByPost, reactionsByPost, attachmentsByPost, pollsByPost] = active === "feed" ? await Promise.all([listRepliesForPosts(ids, ctx.user.id), getPostVotes(ids, ctx.user.id), getPostReactions(ids, ctx.user.id), getPostAttachments(ids), getPostPolls(ids, ctx.user.id)]) : [new Map(), ...empty maps];` Keep the existing conditional listAllEvents/listMemberSpotlight awaits for the other tabs. Also avoid the proposed inline `(await createClient()).rpc('is_admin')` inside the Promise.all array literal — the inner await suspends array construction and partially re-serializes elements after it; hoist the client (as above) or use createClient().then(c => c.rpc('is_admin')).
performance-3.verdictReasoning: Verified in src/app/(app)/community/page.tsx: eight sequential top-level awaits at lines 80 (listSpaces), 85 (listRecentPosts), 90 (listRepliesForPosts), 94 (getPostVotes), 98 (getPostReactions), 102 (getPostAttachments), 106 (getPostPolls), and 119 (is_admin RPC). Only the five per-post helpers depend on post ids from listRecentPosts; listSpaces and is_admin are fully independent, so the optimal shape is 2 serial levels, not 8. Nothing mitigates it: no `use cache`/revalidate/unstable_cache anywhere in the page or src/lib/community/queries.ts; the page is fully dynamic (cookie-bound Supabase server client created per call), each helper issues its own PostgREST HTTP round trip, and Next 16 does not auto-parallelize sequential awaits in a server component. getShellContext is React.cache'd but covers only the shell query. Severity downgraded: the helpers are already bulk (.in()) so there is no N+1 or scaling cliff — this is a fixed, bounded ~5-6 avoidable serial round trips (~150-450 ms depending on Supabase region) of blocking SSR latency on the default community tab. Real and worth fixing, but a bounded latency cost with no correctness/security/growth dimension is medium, not high.

performance-4.title: Program detail page: 4 sequential awaits plus duplicated curriculum queries
performance-4.description: Two issues on /programs/[slug]: (1) after the Promise.all at lines 181-184, the page awaits four independent fetches strictly in series — getProgramUserTasks (line 213), the program_progress enrolled count (lines 219-224), getProgramNotes (line 229), getProgramLearningPoints (line 236). All four only need programUuid/ctx.user.id, adding ~4 serial round trips. No schema or route changes.
performance-4.correctedFix: Step 1 of the proposed fix is correct as written: wrap the four independent fetches (lines 210-237) in one Promise.all with programUuid-guarded fallbacks. Step 2 (derive progress from getCurriculumForProgram's modules) is NOT behavior-preserving and should not be done as proposed — three semantic differences: (a) in queries.ts line 116-122 the status ternary puts proGated before completed, so a non-pro user's completed pro lessons render as "locked"; deriving percent from lesson statuses undercounts vs getProgramProgress, which counts completion across all lessons regardless of plan; (b) when a program exists but lessons aren't seeded, getProgramProgress returns lessonsTotal = program.total_lessons (>0) so effectivePercent (page line 188-189) is the real 0, whereas empty modules would flip it to the demo 62%; (c) getProgramProgress.nextLesson is the first incomplete lesson even if pro-gated, while the curriculum "current" skips gated lessons, changing continueSlug for downgraded users. Safer dedupe: pass the already-fetched dbProgram.id and ctx.user.id into both helpers (eliminating the 3 redundant programs-by-slug lookups and the 3 redundant auth.getUser network calls), or merge them into one helper that fetches lessons + lesson_progress once and returns { modules, progress } using getProgramProgress's ungated counting semantics and total_lessons fallback.
performance-4.verdictReasoning: Both parts reproduce exactly. (1) page.tsx awaits four independent fetches strictly in series after the Promise.all: getProgramUserTasks (line 213, takes only programId/userId — verified in lesson-task-queries.ts), program_progress count (219-224), getProgramNotes (229), getProgramLearningPoints (236). None consumes another's output; ~5 serial round trips (getProgramNotes internally does auth.getUser then the query) that could run concurrently. (2) getCurriculumForProgram (queries.ts 41-142) and getProgramProgress (144-221) each run programs-by-slug, lessons-by-program, auth.getUser, and lesson_progress — and the page itself also queries programs by slug at lines 159-163, so the slug lookup happens 3x per render (claim slightly undercounts). However, the duplicated helper queries run inside Promise.all, so they cost duplicate DB/auth load, not latency; the serial block costs ~100-400ms TTFB depending on DB proximity. No correctness impact, no unbounded N+1. Real and worth fixing on a hot page, but 'high' overstates a bounded few-hundred-ms latency + redundant-load issue — medium is right.

performance-5.title: getOnboardingGate adds up to 5 serial queries per request on programs/tutorials surfaces

performance-10.title: Community feed 'Viewed by' row fetches fake avatars from i.pravatar.cc

performance-11.title: Layout-property animations: flex-basis accordion and height-based progress fill
performance-11.description: Two animations animate layout properties instead of transform: (1) proven-results.tsx lines 116-122 transitions flex-basis (16% ↔ 100%) on four 80vh panels over 0.6s — every hover re-runs full-section layout+paint each frame; the panels contain blurred decorations (blur-[90px] span at line 145) that repaint during the transition, which can visibly jank on mid-range laptops. performance-12.title: Portal menus reposition via non-rAF scroll handlers that setState every scroll event
performance-12.description: status-pill.tsx lines 93-94 and item-actions-menu.tsx lines 126-127 attach capture-phase window scroll + resize listeners (no passive flag, no rAF batching) whose handler (`place`/`reposition`) calls getBoundingClientRect and setState on every scroll event while a row menu is open. On the posting table this re-renders the menu component per scroll tick. Contrast with the marketing scroll sections (stacked-features.tsx lines 107-113, how-it-works.tsx lines 65-72) which correctly cancel/queue through requestAnimationFrame with passive listeners. Impact is small (only while a menu is open) but it is the one place in the app violating the pattern.

Cancel the pending frame in the cleanup.

Because Next code-splits per route this only affects the internal /design gallery itself, but that page parses/hydrates everything for whichever single section is being viewed. Internal-only surface, hence low severity.

logic-auth-security-1.title: Open redirect in /auth/callback via unvalidated ?next= param
logic-auth-security-1.description: The OAuth/magic-link/recovery callback builds its post-exchange destination as `return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}${next}`)` (lines 8-17) where `next` comes straight from the query string with no validation. Because `origin` already ends after `https://host`, an attacker-supplied `next` such as `@evil.com` resolves to `https://host@evil.com` (host=evil.com) and `.evil.com` resolves to `https://host.evil.com` — both are open redirects to an attacker domain. This is inconsistent with the rest of the auth flow: src/app/(auth)/actions.ts (safeInternalPath, lines 16-25) and src/app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx (lines 27-32) both validate the redirect target is a relative path. Exploitation requires a valid one-time auth `code` (so it pairs with a login-CSRF: attacker requests a reset on their own account, appends a malicious next, and lures a victim), which keeps it below critical, but the fix is trivial and the inconsistency is a real hole.
logic-auth-security-1.fix: In src/app/auth/callback/route.ts, validate `next` the same way the sign-in flow does before using it: after computing `next`, replace it with a fallback unless it is a safe internal path, e.g. `const safeNext = next.startsWith('/') && !next.startsWith('//') ? next : (type === 'recovery' ? '/reset-password' : '/dashboard');` and redirect to `${origin}${safeNext}`.

logic-auth-security-2.title: Avatar/banner upload validated client-side only; saveAvatarUrl/saveBannerUrl trust an arbitrary URL
logic-auth-security-2.description: Avatar/banner files are uploaded directly from the browser to the public `community-media` Supabase bucket in uploadUserImage() (settings-panel.tsx lines 200-231), where the only type/size checks are `file.type.startsWith('image/')` and `file.size > 5MB` — both client-side and trivially bypassable by calling the storage API directly. The server actions saveAvatarUrl/saveBannerUrl (settings/actions.ts lines 95-141) then persist whatever URL string the client passes with no validation that it is a community-media URL inside the user's own folder. Migration 0050_community_post_media.sql scopes bucket WRITES to the user's own folder (storage.foldername(name)[1] = auth.uid()) but enforces no allowed_mime_types/size server-side, and SELECT is world-readable. Net effect: a user can store arbitrary file types/sizes (e.g. SVG/HTML) in a public bucket, and can set their stored avatar_url to any external URL (rendered as across the app and the public media-kit page).
logic-auth-security-2.fix: Harden in two places: (1) In saveAvatarUrl/saveBannerUrl (settings/actions.ts), reject any URL that is not a community-media public URL under `${user.id}/` — parse the URL and require it to start with the project's Supabase storage public prefix and contain the caller's user id as the first path segment. (2) Configure allowed_mime_types and file_size_limit on the community-media bucket. Keep the existing client checks as UX only.

logic-auth-security-3.title: Tasks cron route uses non-constant-time secret comparison
logic-auth-security-3.description: The authorized() helper (lines 21-27) compares the bearer token with plain `===` (`header === `Bearer ${secret}` || header === secret`), which is not timing-safe. The sibling cron route src/app/api/admin/emails/run-scheduled/route.ts (lines 25-38) correctly uses node:crypto timingSafeEqual with a length check. This is a minor secret-comparison timing side-channel and an inconsistency between two endpoints that share the same CRON_SECRET.
logic-auth-security-3.fix: Mirror the emails route: import { timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto', strip the optional 'Bearer ' prefix, build Buffers for the provided token and CRON_SECRET, length-check, then timingSafeEqual. Keep the existing 'no secret → refuse' behaviour.

logic-auth-security-4.title: Raw Postgres/Supabase error messages surfaced to end users
logic-auth-security-4.description: Many user-facing server actions return `error.message` straight from PostgREST/Supabase to the client UI, leaking internal schema details (table/column names, constraint names, raw SQLSTATE wording). Examples: monetization/actions.ts returns `{ ok:false, error: error.message }` for every brand-deal/revenue/media-kit failure (e.g. lines 39, 110, 131, 149, 184, 202); community/actions.ts does the same on most inserts (e.g. lines 67, 110, 177); settings/actions.ts returns error.message on profile/pillar failures (lines 31-36, 68, 75, 86, 111, 136). Some sibling code already humanizes known codes (admin/posting/actions.ts humanize(), tasks/actions.ts MISSING_TABLE map), so the pattern is inconsistent. Low severity (info disclosure, no direct exploit) but pervasive and easy to tighten.
logic-auth-security-4.fix: Introduce a small shared helper that maps known codes (42P01/42703/etc.) to friendly text and returns a generic 'Something went wrong, please try again.' for everything else, logging the raw error server-side with console.error. Apply it at the return sites in the cited files instead of passing error.message to the client.

logic-auth-security-5.title: Support ticket reply ownership enforced only by RLS, not at the action layer
logic-auth-security-5.description: addTicketMessage (lines 171-194) inserts a message with a client-supplied `ticketId` and `author:'user'` after only checking that the caller is signed in — it does not verify the ticket belongs to the caller in code. This is currently SAFE because the RLS policy support_messages_insert_own (supabase/migrations/0013_support.sql lines 198-207) requires `author='user' AND the ticket's user_id = auth.uid()`, so a user cannot post on another user's ticket. Flagging as defense-in-depth only: closeTicket() in the same file (lines 200-215) does scope with .eq('user_id', user.id), so addTicketMessage is the odd one out and would silently become an IDOR if that RLS policy were ever dropped/modified.
logic-auth-security-5.fix: Before inserting in addTicketMessage, look up the ticket by id and confirm its user_id === user.id (or pass ticket public_id and resolve with .eq('user_id', user.id)), returning a 'Ticket not found' error otherwise — matching the scoping already used in closeTicket.

logic-auth-security-6.title: OAuth start redirects unauthenticated users with ?next= but sign-in reads ?redirect=
logic-auth-security-6.description: When an unauthenticated request hits the OAuth start route it redirects to `/sign-in?next=/performance` (lines 75-77). The sign-in page and action only read the `redirect`/`redirect_to` param (src/app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx lines 27-32; src/app/(auth)/actions.ts line 33), and the middleware sets `?redirect=` (src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts line 56). So `next` is ignored and the user lands on /dashboard instead of returning to /performance to retry the connection. Low impact because /performance is auth-gated so this path is rarely reached unauthenticated, but it is a real param-name mismatch / dead post-login return.
logic-auth-security-6.fix: In src/app/api/oauth/[platform]/start/route.ts change the sign-in redirect query key from `next` to `redirect` so it matches the sign-in flow: `new URL('/sign-in?redirect=/performance', ...)`.

flows-forms-qa-1.title: Stripe checkout success/cancel return URLs point at /billing, which 308-redirects and silently drops the ?status param
flows-forms-qa-1.description: checkout/route.ts sets success_url=`${appUrl}/billing?status=success` and cancel_url=`${appUrl}/billing?status=cancelled` (lines 66-67). But /billing is now a hard `redirect("/settings/payment-methods")` (billing/page.tsx line 12), and BillingPageClient never reads a `status` searchParam anyway. After paying, the user lands on the billing settings page with NO success confirmation and a stale plan (the webhook may not have synced yet), so the page can still show 'Free'. The advertised post-checkout feedback loop is dead.
flows-forms-qa-1.fix: Change success_url/cancel_url in checkout/route.ts to `${appUrl}/settings/payment-methods?status=success` and `...?status=cancelled`. Then in billing-panel.tsx (or payment-methods/page.tsx) read the `status` searchParam and render a success/cancel banner. Keep the redirect target consistent with the real billing home.
flows-forms-qa-1.correctedFix: The proposed fix is directionally correct but needs two refinements. (1) Point success_url/cancel_url at `${appUrl}/settings/payment-methods?status=success|cancelled` (consider also appending `session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` for server-side verification). (2) Add the missing consumer — none exists today: read `searchParams` in settings/payment-methods/page.tsx (server side) and pass a `checkoutStatus` prop to BillingPageClient, or use useSearchParams in billing-panel.tsx wrapped in Suspense. (3) Word the success banner as 'Payment received — your plan will update in a moment' (and ideally trigger a refresh/poll or verify the checkout session server-side), NOT 'You are now on Pro', because the webhook race means the DB plan can still read Free at render time; a banner asserting the upgrade while the hero shows 'Free plan' would be contradictory. Note the claim's '308' detail is wrong — billing/page.tsx uses redirect() which is a 307 (the file comment saying 'permanent redirect' is also inaccurate) — but the query param is dropped either way.
flows-forms-qa-1.verdictReasoning: Verified in code: checkout/route.ts:66-67 sets success_url/cancel_url to `${appUrl}/billing?status=...`; src/app/(app)/billing/page.tsx:12 is `redirect("/settings/payment-methods")`, which per this Next build's own docs (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/redirect.md) emits a 307 (not 308 — minor claim error; permanentRedirect is the 308 variant) with a bare-path Location, so `?status=...` is dropped. src/proxy.ts does not handle /billing or preserve queries, and a repo-wide grep shows NO code anywhere reads a `status` search param — neither BillingPageClient (billing-panel.tsx) nor settings/payment-methods/page.tsx — so the post-checkout feedback loop is genuinely dead (in fact it was already dead before the /billing move, since the param never had a consumer). The stale-plan concern is also real: payment-methods/page.tsx renders ctx.plan from the DB, which only the Stripe webhook updates, so a paying user can land back on a page still showing 'Free' with a live 'Upgrade to Pro' button and zero confirmation. However, 'high' overstates it: the payment, webhook sync, and eventual plan display all work correctly; this is a confirmation/UX-trust gap (with some risk of a confused re-checkout attempt), not broken billing, data corruption, or security — medium severity.

flows-forms-qa-3.title: Plan displayed in Settings/Billing reads profiles.plan, but the Stripe webhook only writes subscriptions.plan — plan badges can be permanently stale
flows-forms-qa-3.description: The plan shown on the Settings profile card (settings-panel.tsx line 257, PLAN_META) and the sidebar/topbar all come from `profiles.plan` via getShellContext (get-shell-context.ts line 32). On upgrade/downgrade the Stripe webhook's syncSubscriptionRow only updates the `subscriptions` table (route.ts lines 186-199) and handleSubscriptionDeleted likewise resets only `subscriptions` (lines 83-91) — neither touches `profiles.plan`. The only code that writes profiles.plan is the admin action (admin/users/[id]/actions.ts). There is no DB trigger syncing subscriptions.plan→profiles.plan (grep of migrations finds none). Result: a real customer who upgrades to Pro via Stripe keeps showing 'Free plan' on their profile/sidebar indefinitely, while the /billing page (which reads getSubscription→subscriptions table) correctly shows Pro — an inconsistent, confusing split-brain. The billing-panel itself is fed `ctx.plan` (from profiles) for the hero/compare cards, so even the billing page's plan badge is wrong while invoices/status are right.
flows-forms-qa-3.fix: In webhooks/stripe/route.ts syncSubscriptionRow and handleSubscriptionDeleted, also update profiles.plan for the same user (e.g. add `await supabase.from('profiles').update({ plan }).eq('id', userId)` alongside the subscriptions update). This is a missing-write fix, not a schema change.
flows-forms-qa-3.correctedFix: The proposed dual-write is directionally correct (it mirrors the existing admin action in admin/users/[id]/actions.ts which already writes both tables), but as stated it is slightly incomplete: customer.subscription.updated also fires for non-entitled statuses (incomplete, incomplete_expired, unpaid), so unconditionally writing the paid plan to profiles.plan could grant Pro gating without a successful payment. In syncSubscriptionRow, derive the profile plan from status, e.g. const entitled = ["active","trialing","past_due"].includes(subscription.status); await supabase.from("profiles").update({ plan: entitled ? plan : "free" }).eq("id", userId); and in handleSubscriptionDeleted add await supabase.from("profiles").update({ plan: "free" }).eq("id", userId). (Service-role client bypasses RLS, so both writes succeed.) Longer term, consider making subscriptions the single source of truth and dropping profiles.plan reads, but the guarded dual-write is the right minimal fix.
flows-forms-qa-3.verdictReasoning: Every element of the claim reproduces in the code. (1) get-shell-context.ts:32 derives plan solely from profiles.plan; ctx.plan feeds the sidebar/topbar (src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:34,39), the Settings profile card (settings-panel.tsx:257 PLAN_META[profile?.plan ?? "free"]), and the billing UI itself (settings/payment-methods/page.tsx:31 passes plan={ctx.plan} to BillingPageClient, whose SubscriptionOverview and ComparePlansSection render from that prop while invoices/status come from the subscriptions table — the split-brain described). (2) The Stripe webhook writes only the subscriptions table: syncSubscriptionRow (route.ts:186-199) and handleSubscriptionDeleted (route.ts:82-91); the checkout route writes nothing plan-related to profiles. (3) Repo-wide grep confirms the only profiles.plan writer is the admin action (admin/users/[id]/actions.ts:34-42), which tellingly dual-writes both profiles AND subscriptions — proof the columns are intended to mirror each other. (4) Migrations 0001-0055 contain no trigger/function syncing subscriptions.plan → profiles.plan; the only triggers on public.subscriptions are touch_updated_at (0001_init.sql:292-294). No middleware/proxy or framework behavior is relevant. The impact is actually WORSE than claimed: ctx.plan also drives paid-content gating — tutorials/page.tsx:83 → library.tsx:315 (proLocked) and programs/[slug]/page.tsx:182 → programs/queries.ts:114 (proGated lessons marked "locked") — so a paying Stripe Pro customer is permanently locked out of Pro tutorials/lessons, not just shown a stale badge, until an admin manually edits their plan. The webhook uses createServiceClient (service role), so RLS does not block the proposed write. Severity high is justified (paid-feature denial for real customers); keeping rather than upgrading since an admin workaround exists and it only affects post-Stripe-checkout flows.

flows-forms-qa-2.title: Onboarding completion screen can dead-end users who never finish (or whose browser cannot play) the intro video except via a graceful-fail path
flows-forms-qa-2.description: On the final onboarding step the 'Go to platform' button is hard-gated on `introWatched` (complete.tsx lines 118-120). `introWatched` only flips true when the video reaches its end OR onError fires (intro-video.tsx markComplete). The real asset is /onboarding-intro.mp4 which is not committed; if it 404s, onError unlocks the flow — fine. But if the asset IS present and the user simply pauses/abandons it, the ONLY way forward is to fully watch it (scrubbing past max-watched is blocked). There is no skip affordance and the profile is already saved (`onboarded:true`), so a user who closes the tab is now `onboarded` yet never reached the dashboard via this screen — on next login AppLayout sees onboarded=true and sends them to /dashboard, so they silently never see the celebration. The gate adds friction with no escape hatch for users who can't/won't watch.
flows-forms-qa-2.fix: Add a low-emphasis 'Skip intro' link next to the gated button in complete.tsx that calls router.push('/dashboard'), or unlock the button after a max wait. The profile is already persisted so skipping is safe.

flows-forms-qa-4.title: requestPasswordReset builds the reset link from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL defaulting to localhost:3000, but the app runs on :8080
flows-forms-qa-4.description: requestPasswordReset (actions.ts lines 143-147) sets redirectTo=`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'}/auth/callback?type=recovery&next=/reset-password`. The onboarding welcome-email code (onboarding/actions.ts lines 107-110) instead derives the host from the request headers, and the billing routes also fall back to localhost:3000. If NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is unset in this environment the password-reset email link points at :3000 while the dev server is :8080 — the reset link 404s/cannot reach the running app, breaking the forgot→reset flow end to end. The fallback is also inconsistent with the header-derived approach used elsewhere.
flows-forms-qa-4.fix: Either ensure NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is set, or derive the origin from request headers (await headers()) as onboarding/actions.ts already does, instead of hardcoding localhost:3000. Confirm the configured value matches the runtime port.

flows-forms-qa-5.title: Settings 'Personal details' Save omits the displayed Email/Category/Handle and treats follower_base 'Select range…' (empty) as a deletion silently
flows-forms-qa-5.description: saveProfileSettings only persists full_name, phone, follower_base (actions.ts lines 8-40). The follower_base Select includes an empty 'Select range…' option (settings-panel.tsx FOLLOWER_OPTIONS line 91). If a user with an existing follower_base accidentally re-selects the blank option and presses Save, follower_base is overwritten with '' — wiping their audience size and the 'X followers' line on the profile header with no warning. There's also no client-side validation gate; the Save button is always enabled. Minor data-loss footgun.
flows-forms-qa-5.fix: In settings-panel.tsx handleSave (or saveProfileSettings), skip writing follower_base when the value is '' (treat the placeholder as 'no change'), or remove the empty option from the editable Select. Keep the placeholder for display-only.

flows-forms-qa-6.title: CreatorBrand 'Platform & audience' Save re-writes ALL content pillars even though that section never edits pillars
flows-forms-qa-6.description: Both the 'Creator brand' and 'Platform & audience' save buttons call the same handleSave→saveCreatorInfo with the full payload {bio, niche, primary_platform, pillars} (settings-panel.tsx lines 612-632; both SettingRow Save buttons at 805 and 904). saveCreatorInfo unconditionally DELETEs all content_pillars then re-inserts from the passed array (actions.ts lines 71-87). The two cards share one `pillars` state, so saving 'Platform & audience' is harmless when pillars are in sync — but because the delete+reinsert is not atomic and runs on every save of either section, an error between the delete and insert (insErr path) leaves the user with zero pillars and returns an error, with no rollback. Editing platform should not be able to nuke pillars.
flows-forms-qa-6.fix: Split saveCreatorInfo so the platform/niche save does NOT touch content_pillars (only update profiles), and only the brand/pillars save manages pillars. Alternatively wrap delete+insert in a single RPC/transaction so a mid-operation failure can't leave pillars empty.

flows-forms-qa-7.title: Language & region settings 'Save' persists region only to localStorage and is never read anywhere — the setting does nothing
flows-forms-qa-7.description: The Region & date format selector writes to localStorage key 'cgos:region' (language-form.tsx lines 12,38) and shows a 'Saved' confirmation, but a repo-wide grep shows 'cgos:region' is read by NOTHING else — no date/number formatting consumes it. The UI promises 'Controls how dates and numbers appear' (line 88) yet changing the region has zero effect anywhere in the app. The language half works (cookie + reload), but the region control is a button wired to a no-op store.
flows-forms-qa-7.fix: Either wire the region value into the date/number formatters that render throughout the app (read 'cgos:region' where toLocaleDateString is used), or remove the region selector and its 'Controls how dates and numbers appear' copy until it's implemented.

flows-forms-qa-8.title: Onboarding Pro→Stripe handoff swallows checkout failures and silently lands the user on the success screen as Free
flows-forms-qa-8.description: In flow.tsx submit() (lines 69-88), when the user picked Pro and stripeReady is true, it POSTs /api/billing/checkout. If res is not ok or has no url, the code falls through to setStep('complete') with NO message — the button said 'Start 7-day free trial' / 'Starting your trial…', but the user silently ends up onboarded on Free with no indication checkout failed. The catch block is likewise empty (line 85). The user believes they started a Pro trial when they didn't.
flows-forms-qa-8.fix: In the non-ok / catch branches, surface a non-blocking notice (e.g. setSubmitError('We couldn’t start your Pro trial — you’re set up on Free; upgrade anytime from Billing.')) before falling through to the complete screen, so the user knows the trial didn't start.

flows-forms-qa-9.title: Community chat: failed sends surface a transient 4s toast but the typed message + pending image are discarded on the next attempt's success only — no optimistic echo, and reconnect refetch can drop the user's own un-acked message
flows-forms-qa-9.description: Composer.submit() (composer.tsx lines 173-191) only clears the textarea/image AFTER a successful sendMessage; on failure it calls onError(result.error) which shows a 4-second auto-dismissing toast (chat-room.tsx showError, line 78-82) and keeps the text — that part is OK. The real gap: there is no optimistic message insert, so when the network is slow the user sees nothing happen until the round-trip + realtime INSERT lands. Worse, the send button is disabled while !isConnected (line 301) but if the socket drops mid-send and reconnects, the reconnect-recovery refetch (chat-room.tsx lines 201-209) only ADDS messages it doesn't already have — a message the server accepted during the gap will appear, but a message the client THINKS it sent (and cleared) but that errored will be silently lost with only a 4s toast as evidence. For a chat feature this is a fragile delivery story.
flows-forms-qa-9.fix: Add an optimistic pending-message bubble keyed by a client id, reconcile it against the realtime INSERT, and on send failure keep the draft AND show a persistent retry affordance instead of a 4s toast. At minimum, make the error toast persistent (not auto-dismiss) when a send fails so the user isn't misled into thinking it went through.

flows-forms-qa-10.title: Onboarding gate locks lessons but Pro-only lock CTA links to /billing?upgrade=pro, which redirects and drops the upgrade hint
flows-forms-qa-10.description: The Pro-locked lesson CTA links to `/billing?upgrade=pro` (lessonSlug/page.tsx line 267). /billing 308-redirects to /settings/payment-methods (billing/page.tsx), dropping the `upgrade=pro` query param, and BillingPageClient never reads it anyway — so the deep-link intent (auto-scroll to / highlight the Pro upgrade) is lost. The user just lands on the generic billing page. Same pattern as the checkout return-URL issue.
flows-forms-qa-10.fix: Point the CTA at /settings/payment-methods (and optionally add ?upgrade=pro handling in billing-panel to expand/scroll the Compare plans section). Audit other `/billing?...` links (command palette, profile menu) for the same dropped-param problem.

flows-forms-qa-11.title: Support new-ticket page rejects topic 'other' that the server action and ticket-detail rendering both accept
flows-forms-qa-11.description: new/page.tsx VALID_TOPIC_KEYS (lines 30-39) lists 8 topics and excludes 'other', so a deep-link like /support/new?topic=other is silently dropped to undefined. But the server action's VALID_TOPICS (actions.ts lines 24-27) DOES include 'other', and the ticket-detail page maps topics through SUPPORT_TOPICS. This is a minor inconsistency: 'other' is a first-class topic everywhere except the deep-link parser, so it can never be pre-selected via URL even though it's a valid value.
flows-forms-qa-11.fix: Add 'other' to VALID_TOPIC_KEYS in new/page.tsx to match the server action's VALID_TOPICS, keeping the topic list consistent across the wizard, the action, and the detail view.

flows-forms-qa-12.title: Profile/avatar saves call revalidatePath('/settings') but the billing & connected-accounts settings subpages won't reflect updated profile data until a hard reload
flows-forms-qa-12.description: saveProfileSettings/saveCreatorInfo/saveAvatarUrl/saveBannerUrl all revalidatePath('/settings') only (actions.ts lines 38,89,114,139). The settings live across multiple routes (/settings, /settings/payment-methods, /settings/connected-accounts, etc.) all wrapped by settings/layout.tsx, and the sidebar/topbar (driven by getShellContext) show name/avatar/plan. Updating the avatar revalidates /settings but not the shell layout, so the just-changed avatar in the topbar (Topbar uses ctx.topUser.avatar_url) won't update until a navigation/reload — the local component state updates the on-page avatar but the chrome lags. Cosmetic staleness rather than data loss.
flows-forms-qa-12.fix: Add `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` (or revalidate the relevant settings subpaths) to the avatar/banner/profile save actions so the app-shell topbar avatar refreshes in step with the on-page change.
